links.outcome: Readability (SMOG reading grade level) of chatbot responses to head and neck cancer symptom queries
links.effect: Copilot had the lowest mean SMOG of 12.56 (95% CI 11.82 to 13.31); Open Evidence was highest at 17.49 (95% CI 16.66 to 18.31), a graduate reading level.
links.quote: Open Evidence scored lowest in both quality averaging 30.52 (95 % CI: 27.52 to 33.52) and readability of 17.49 (95 % CI: 16.66 to 18.31), reflecting a graduate reading level.

links.outcome: Reading level of AI-generated patient-facing responses relative to appropriate patient reading level
links.effect: Even the most readable platform (Copilot) scored a mean SMOG of 12.56, above typical patient reading levels; Open Evidence reached 17.49 (graduate level).
links.quote: Microsoft Copilot achieved the highest mean DISCERN score of 41.40 (95 % CI: 40.31 to 42.49) and the lowest mean SMOG reading levels of 12.56 (95 % CI: 11.82 to 13.31), outperforming ChatGPT, Google Gemini, and Open Evidence in overall quality and accessibility (p < .001).

screen.reason: Evaluates the quality and readability (DISCERN and SMOG) of four commercial LLM chatbots on 25 simulated patient queries regarding head and neck cancer symptoms without testing a specific organizational guardrail or deployment practice.
